attrs.gap: OPEN AS AN EXISTENTIAL, and GPT-5.6 ruled at R7.4 that this is the right state for it: it asks whether SOME semantics-preserving compilation exists, which nothing has refuted. Its coverage-level instance is separate and REFUTED — ASR-CURRENT-COMPILE-FAITHFUL. R7.4 ALSO REGENERATED THIS TEXT, WHICH WAS STALE: it described TWO readings with `eliminative` primary, and the running artifact has computed THREE since R6.1 with `active_unresolved` primary, disagreeing on 22 record-level pairs rather than the 1 defeater and 5 assurance states named here. The explanation had been describing an older experiment for three rounds, in a record whose subject is whether a description matches what runs. Before this can be answered at all, ASR-NATIVE-SEMANTICS has to exist: at present the labels are produced BY the AF, so `preserving` has no independent referent.

attrs.prior_art: Modgil & Prakken, The ASPIC+ framework for structured argumentation (2014) — structured arguments and typed attacks are compiled into a Dung defeat framework, and the preference ordering is what turns an attack into a defeat. Cayrol & Lagasquie-Schiex on bipolar argumentation, and Oren & Norman's evidential argumentation systems (COMMA 2008), where an argument is unacceptable unless supported by evidence — the closest prior art to a mosaic whose support must bottom out in instruments.
